about: The current El Niño outlook, shared by the El Niño watch on /signals/, the explainer at /el-nino/, the guide at /el-nino-and-cities/ and the printable briefing (read through tools/enso-outlook.js, which also checks this record and supplies the sentences every page repeats). Each entry keeps the issuer's own issue date, forecast period, geography and index; entries with different indices or baselines are never combined or averaged. Every entry names the claims it rests on in research/2026-11/enso-asia/claims.json or research/2026-11/enso-update/claims.json; the build stops if one has not passed the source check. To update: stage the new bulletin in a batch, run verify-sources.yml and the batch's gate.js, move the superseded entry to 'history', then edit this file. 'checked' is the editorial check date: it appears in source details and metadata only, never as a date the content was added. A failed fetch changes nothing here: the last verified bulletin stays until a newer one is confirmed.

status.label: El Niño Advisory
status.means: NOAA's alert status when El Niño conditions are observed and expected to continue.
status.observed: El Niño strengthened compared with the previous month: sea surface temperature anomalies exceeded 4.0 °C and extended farther west across the eastern equatorial Pacific. The weekly Niño-3.4 index reached +2.5 °C, and rainfall stayed suppressed over Indonesia.
status.forecast: A strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January to March 2027 (a greater than 79% chance), before it begins to weaken in early 2027.
status.observed_basis: NOAA's monthly review of conditions in the tropical Pacific. The +2.5 °C Niño-3.4 figure is the latest weekly value it reports, not the three-month RONI used to classify events.

archive.label: NOAA's archived copy of this discussion

phase.title: Official ENSO probabilities
phase.index: Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI), Niño-3.4 region, 1991–2020 base, ±0.5 °C thresholds

others.title: ENSO: Recent Evolution, Current Status and Predictions (weekly update)
others.index: Weekly Niño indices and RONI (weekly values are not three-month indices)
others.says: A weekly monitoring summary between monthly discussions, not a new outlook. Suppressed convection and rainfall has persisted over Indonesia since June 2026.

others.title: Climate driver update: ENSO and the Indian Ocean
others.period: week ending 22 November 2026; outlook to March to May 2027 (southern autumn)
others.index: Weekly relative Niño3.4 (not RONI); weekly Indian Ocean Dipole index
others.says: Weekly relative Niño3.4 of +2.67 °C for the week ending 22 November 2026, below the event's peak so far of +2.88 °C. Most models expect warming to peak in December or January and to stay above El Niño thresholds into the southern autumn of 2027 (March to May 2027). The Bureau notes that a strong Niño3.4 signal does not necessarily mean strong impacts.

others.title: Regional Climate: El Niño / La Niña (status with October 2026 values)
others.period: October 2026, and August to October 2026; outlook to April 2027
others.geography: Niño3.4 region, read for Southeast Asia
others.index: Relative Niño3.4; RONI (three-month); events classified at ±0.65 °C
others.says: Relative Niño3.4 of 2.3 °C for October 2026 and 2.0 °C for August to October 2026. The index is predicted to peak during November to December 2026; strong El Niño conditions are predicted to persist until February to March 2027, with El Niño continuing until at least March to April 2027; most models (more than 70%) predict El Niño will still be present in April 2027.

others.title: ENSO and IOD Bulletin, October 2026
others.period: September 2026; outlook through January to March 2027
others.geography: Tropical Pacific and Indian Ocean, read for India
others.index: Niño 3.4 SST anomaly, ±0.5 °C (Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecast System, September 2026 start); Dipole Mode Index, ±0.4 °C
others.says: A high likelihood of strong-to-very strong El Niño conditions persisting through January to March 2027. Neutral Indian Ocean Dipole conditions prevail and are most likely to continue; IMD notes some international centres expect the positive phase to continue in the near term. This was IMD's latest bulletin online on 26 November 2026.

others.title: Global Seasonal Climate Update for November 2026 to January 2027
others.geography: Niño 3.4 region and the Indian Ocean
others.index: Niño 3.4 sea surface temperature anomaly, multi-model ensemble mean (not RONI)
others.says: The seasonal average anomaly is forecast at about +3.8 °C, peaking around December 2026; a positive Indian Ocean Dipole is forecast to decline to +0.3 °C.

others.title: El Niño/La Niña Update (WMO's latest quarterly update; no newer one was found by 26 November 2026)
others.index: Consensus of WMO Global Producing Centres
others.says: An exceptionally high likelihood, nearly 100%, that El Niño persists through February 2027.

others.title: Seasonal forecast for November 2026 to January 2027
others.says: Below-normal rainfall over parts of the southeastern and northeastern Maritime Continent and southeastern mainland Southeast Asia, and above-normal temperature over the ASEAN region. National services hold the national-scale outlook.

interpretation: The odds favour El Niño persisting into the start of the hot season in much of South and Southeast Asia, then easing. That is a reason to get ordinary heat protection working early, in the places where people already spend the hottest hours. It is not a forecast of a heatwave anywhere.
local_uncertainty: A Pacific probability is not any town's chance of a heatwave, a water shortage or a flood. NOAA's strength odds describe the Pacific index, not the strength of local impacts. Local outcomes depend on the season, geography, other drivers such as the Indian Ocean Dipole, long-term warming and local conditions; national seasonal outlooks and official local warnings carry that detail.

history.title: El Niño/La Niña status
history.says: The relative Niño3.4 index was 2.1 °C for September and 1.7 °C for July to September, and was predicted to peak during October to December 2026.

iod.text: Agencies read the Indian Ocean Dipole differently, because each uses its own index and threshold. The Bureau of Meteorology reports a weekly index of +0.53 °C for the week ending 22 November 2026 and expects the positive event to weaken and return to neutral in early southern summer; ASMC expects positive conditions to return to neutral in January 2027; IMD's October bulletin reports neutral conditions on its ±0.4 °C threshold. Read each with its own date; they are not averaged.

unchanged.text: No substantive change since NOAA's discussion of 12 November 2026: no newer monthly discussion has been issued (the next is due 10 December 2026). NOAA's weekly update of 23 November, the Bureau of Meteorology's weekly values to 22 November and ASMC's status page are consistent with it. WMO's update of 20 November 2026 is a project update on preparedness, not a new forecast.
